name: config
description: Spring physics configuration that controls animation behavior. React-spring uses real spring physics simulation (not time-based easing) for natural, realistic motion.

parameters.name: mass
parameters.description: Spring mass (weight). Higher mass = slower movement, more momentum. Think: heavy vs. light objects.
parameters.physics: Increases inertia. Heavy springs take longer to accelerate and decelerate.

parameters.name: tension
parameters.description: Spring stiffness. Higher tension = faster, snappier animations. Think: tight vs. loose rubber band.
parameters.physics: Force that pulls spring toward target. Higher values create faster oscillations.

parameters.name: friction
parameters.description: Spring resistance (damping). Higher friction = less bouncy, more controlled. Think: air resistance.
parameters.physics: Opposes motion and reduces oscillation. Low friction = bouncy, high friction = smooth stop.

parameters.name: bounce
parameters.description: Alternative to friction using bounce coefficient (0 = no bounce, 1 = very bouncy). Easier to tune than friction.
parameters.physics: 0 = critically damped (no overshoot), 0.5 = some bounce, 1 = continuous oscillation

parameters.name: frequency
parameters.description: Alternative to tension. Natural frequency of oscillation in Hz. Easier to reason about than tension.
parameters.physics: How many oscillations per second if no friction. Higher = faster spring.

parameters.name: damping
parameters.description: Alternative to friction using damping ratio. 1 = critically damped (no overshoot), <1 = underdamped (bouncy), >1 = overdamped (sluggish).
parameters.physics: Standard physics term. 1.0 = fastest approach without overshoot. Use with frequency for precise control.

parameters.name: clamp
parameters.description: When true, stops spring at target value (no overshoot). Useful for preventing UI elements from exceeding bounds.
parameters.physics: Disables spring physics at target, converting to linear approach.

parameters.name: precision
parameters.description: Minimum velocity threshold before animation completes. Lower = more accurate but longer animations.
parameters.physics: Defines 'close enough' to target. Prevents infinite tiny movements.

parameters.name: velocity
parameters.description: Initial velocity of the spring. Useful for gesture-based animations that should continue momentum.
parameters.physics: Starting speed. Positive = moving toward target, negative = moving away.

parameters.name: round
parameters.description: Round output values to nearest multiple. E.g., round: 1 = integers only. Prevents sub-pixel rendering.
parameters.physics: Post-processing step, doesn't affect physics simulation.

parameters.name: duration
parameters.description: Use time-based animation instead of spring physics. Overrides mass/tension/friction. Useful for precise timing.
parameters.physics: DISABLES spring physics entirely. Uses easing function over fixed time.

parameters.name: easing
parameters.description: Easing function for duration-based animations. Only works when duration is set. Import from @react-spring/web easings.
parameters.physics: Maps linear time (0-1) to animation progress. Common: easeOutQuad, easeInOutCubic, easeOutBounce.

parameters.name: decay
parameters.description: Natural decay animation (like physics drag). True = auto-calculate, number = custom decay rate. Great for scroll/fling gestures.
parameters.physics: Exponential velocity decay. Initial velocity required. No target value.

presets.name: config.stiff
presets.description: High tension spring - fast and responsive

physicsExplanation.springPhysics: React-spring simulates real spring-damper physics using Hooke's Law (F = -kx) and damping forces. This creates natural, realistic motion that feels responsive to user input.
physicsExplanation.tuningGuidance: Start with presets. For custom tuning: increase tension for faster motion, increase friction to reduce bounce. Or use frequency (Hz) + damping ratio (0-2) for intuitive control.
physicsExplanation.whenToUsePhysics: Use spring physics (default) for interactive UIs, gestures, and natural motion. Springs automatically adapt to interruptions and feel responsive.
physicsExplanation.whenToUseDuration: Use duration-based animations for choreographed sequences, precise timing requirements, or matching design specs. Less natural but more predictable.

commonPatterns: Quick buttons: config.stiff or { tension: 210, friction: 20 }
Smooth modals: config.gentle or { tension: 120, friction: 14 }
Playful interactions: config.wobbly or { tension: 180, friction: 12 }
Slow reveals: config.slow or { duration: 2000, easing: easings.easeOutQuad }
Gesture momentum: { decay: true, velocity: gestureVelocity }
